title: Microscopic Side Information Controls Ordered Hayden--Preskill Recovery
authors: Joao V. R. Alencar, Allan R. P. Moreira, Joao B. R. Silva
abstract: In the Hayden--Preskill protocol, the decoder is usually assumed to know the microscopic identity of the collected output qubits. We study what happens when these labels are unavailable and only the relative order of the received qubits is preserved. The resulting order-preserving deletion channel maps an $n$-qubit scrambled register to a subsequence of length $\ell$. For a diary of fixed size $k$, we prove that the optimal entanglement fidelity converges to the no-output value $4^{-k}$ when $\ell=o(n^{2/3})$, uniformly over the scrambling unitary. For a Haar-random scrambling unitary, it converges to one when $\ell=ω(n^{2/3})$ and $\ell=o(n)$. Monotonicity then gives the fixed-error recovery scale $\ell_{\mathrm{rec}}=Θ(n^{2/3})$. We also consider partial position information obtained by dividing the register into $B$ consecutive blocks and revealing the block of origin of each received qubit. The recovery scale becomes $\ell_{\mathrm{rec}}(n,B)\asymp n^{2/3}B^{-1/3}$ for $B\leq\sqrt n$ and $\ell_{\mathrm{rec}}(n,B)\asymp n/B$ for $B\geq\sqrt n$. The exponent $2/3$ is traced to rank-aligned coincidences between random subsequences, which control both the converse and the recovery argument. Thus, even purely classical information about the origin of the received subsystems can change the amount of quantum output required for Hayden--Preskill recovery.
summary: This paper analyzes the robustness of quantum state recovery (Hayden--Preskill) when side information about the measured qubits is incomplete, such as only knowing their relative order or block origin. It derives precise scaling laws showing that this limited classical information fundamentally changes the required quantum output size needed for successful recovery.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum recovery protocols, specifically the Hayden--Preskill protocol, when the decoder lacks full microscopic identity of output qubits, retaining only relative order or partial block location.
main_result: The optimal entanglement fidelity convergence and the required operational recovery length ($\ell_{	ext{rec}}$) are determined by the type of side information available, yielding critical scaling exponents like $\Theta(n^{2/3})$ for ordered deletion.
method: The analysis employs quantum channel theory, utilizing normalized Choi state purity bounds derived from moment calculations and establishing converse bounds via information-theoretic tools like R\'enyi divergences.
model_or_system: The model is the Hayden--Preskill protocol applied to an $n$-qubit scrambled register. The noise channels considered are ordered deletion (preserving relative order) or block-resolved partial labels, which act on subsequences of qubits.
key_observables: Optimal entanglement fidelity ($F_{	ext{opt}}^e$), recovery length ($\ell_{	ext{rec}}$), and the normalized Choi state purity ($G_{n,\ell}$).
important_parameters: $n$ (total size), $\ell$ (subsequence length), $k$ (diary size), $B$ (number of blocks); critical scaling exponents include $2/3$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the decoder only has access to relative order or block origin information, not absolute positions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the fixed-error recovery phase diagram showing how $\ell_{	ext{rec}}/\sqrt{n}$ scales with $B/\sqrt{n}$ across different asymptotic regimes.
paper_structure: The paper defines protocols and operational quantities (Section II), states the main results for ordered/block-resolved recovery laws (Section III), and details the rigorous proofs using moment estimates and information bounds (Section IV).
why_interesting: While focused on quantum information theory, the analysis of structured noise channels and scaling laws ($\ell_{	ext{rec}} \sim n^{2/3}$) provides general tools for understanding how partial knowledge constrains physical processes in complex quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Scaling form of the fixed-error recovery phase diagram. With x = B/√n, one has ℓrec/√n ≍x−1/3 in the many-survivor-per-block regime and ℓrec/√n ≍x−1 in the sparse-block regime. The two branches meet at B ≍√n and ℓrec ≍√n. The plotted branches represent the two asymptotic scaling regimes; the crossover profile for B/√n = Θ(1) is not determined by these bounds.
